examples.text: De boer perste het sap uit de sinaasappels.
examples.translation: The farmer squeezed the juice out of the oranges.
examples.english: The farmer squeezed the juice out of the oranges.

examples.text: De crimineel perste geld uit zijn slachtoffers door hen te bedreigen.
examples.translation: The criminal extorted money from his victims by threatening them.
examples.english: The criminal extorted money from his victims by threatening them.

forms.form:
te zullen uitpersen
uit te zullen persen

glosses: door persen geheel van vocht ontdoen
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see squeeze, out.

examples.text: Squeeze out some toothpaste and put it on your toothbrush.
Nothing more can be squeezed out of the motive power unit once the master controller has been moved to full on.

glosses: (sports) To force (a competitor) out of one of a limited number of winning positions by taking over that position or a higher one.

examples.text: I auditioned and I would have had the role, but I got squeezed out by a more experienced actor
They came from nowhere to take over second place, squeezing out the previously eighth-place team
Huth headed wide inside two minutes, Andy Wilkinson blasted over from Shotton's cut-back and Jones was squeezed out when bearing down on goal.

glosses: To obtain (a difficult victory) in a competition.

examples.text: The team managed to squeeze out a win in the final minutes.
The team managed to squeeze it out.
